The pilot will test whether it improves digital literacy, reduces technology problems and improves the learning experience for students and families. The pilot runs January 1, 2025 through June 30, 2025, and began before this approval.

output.headline: Applies for up to $4,999,960.16 from the EPA for school water lead testing and water stations
output.summary: The board is approving the district's application to the Environmental Protection Agency for $4,999,960.16 over five years. The money would pay for testing lead in school water, adding FloWater stations and making repairs so lead levels are 5 parts per billion or less. This is an application only; no grant has been awarded yet. The proposed grant period is May 1, 2025 to April 30, 2030.

output.headline: Pays Space80seven up to $58,000 for a work-based internship for ten Fremont High students
output.summary: Space80sevenllc will support a pre-apprenticeship style work-based learning internship with hands-on training for ten students in the Media Academy and Architectural Career Technical Education programs at Fremont High School. The work runs from November 15, 2024 through June 30, 2025, and began before this board vote.

output.headline: Pays Street Academy Foundation up to $24,930.23 for career pathway courses at Emiliano Zapata Street Academy
output.summary: Street Academy Foundation will support student access to courses and experiences in the Education, Child Development and Family Services career pathway at Emiliano Zapata Street Academy. The agreement period began July 1, 2024, before this vote, and runs through June 30, 2025.

output.headline: Pays Therapeutic Beat Making up to $2,400 for music production workshops at Dewey Academy
output.summary: Therapeutic Beat Making, LLC will work with other Today's Future Sound consultants to teach beat making, finger drumming and music production one hour per week at Dewey Academy. Students will produce original tracks for a compilation album with their own cover art. The work runs from December 2, 2024 through May 26, 2025, and began before this board vote.

output.headline: Approves a no-cost pilot of Volt AI software to enhance security with existing cameras
output.summary: Volt AI is giving the district a limited license to try its software at no cost. The pilot would use existing camera feeds to enhance security after hours and on weekends. The pilot runs November 21, 2024 through January 21, 2025, and began before this approval.

output.headline: Pays Langan up to $83,930 for environmental site assessments at seven schools
output.summary: Langan CA will provide environmental site assessment consulting for site improvement projects at seven elementary schools. The cap of $83,930 includes a $7,630 contingency for additional services. The work is expected to run from January 9, 2025 through April 30, 2025.

output.headline: Accepts $650,000 from the Eat.Learn.Play Foundation for emergency water refill stations at schools
output.summary: The district is accepting a $650,000 grant from the Eat.Learn.Play Foundation to install FloWater water stations and provide access to water bottles at school sites. The grant period runs from September 23, 2024 through January 31, 2025. The grant began before this board approval.

output.headline: Pays #ICANHELP up to $8,684 for digital safety training at Oakland Technical High School
output.summary: #ICANHELP will train staff at Oakland Technical High School to teach students digital citizenship and healthy tech and social media habits. It will also give parents and guardians guidance on setting boundaries and modeling good online behavior. The term runs from December 16, 2024 through February 15, 2025, and began before this board vote.

output.headline: Pays Bay Area Community Resources up to $20,000 for a case manager at Rudsdale Continuation High
output.summary: Bay Area Community Resources will provide a daily case manager for students in the Health and Technology pathways at Rudsdale Continuation High School, with a caseload of fifty to sixty at-risk students. It will also train all teachers on trauma-informed practices and develop cultural activities. The agreement period began August 12, 2024, before this vote, and runs through June 30, 2025.

output.headline: Pays Civic Productions up to $15,000 for urban design projects with Castlemont High students
output.summary: Civic Productions LLC will help design curriculum and community projects with students in Castlemont High School's Sustainable Urban Design Academy. Work includes teacher training, field trips to industry sites, a greenhouse and shade house for the school farm, and a digital library of projects. The work runs from October 1, 2024 through June 30, 2025, and began before this board vote.

output.headline: Pays Mentoring Medicine & Science up to $14,290 for health career workshops at Dewey Academy
output.summary: Mentoring Medicine & Science, Inc. will run its Health Scholar Program at Dewey Academy, with workshops each trimester on health careers, emergency medical technicians, CPR and first aid skills. The agreement period ran from August 30 through December 31, 2024, which was before this board vote.

output.headline: Brings International Rescue Committee food bank and cooking class to Oakland International High at no cost
output.summary: The International Rescue Committee will run a food bank every Tuesday and an after-school cooking class every Wednesday at Oakland International High School. The agreement runs from November 25, 2024 through June 30, 2025, at no cost to the district, and began before this board vote.

output.headline: Pays a music instructor up to $3,600 for beat making workshops at Dewey Academy
output.summary: An individual instructor will teach beat making and music production workshops at Dewey Academy, working with Today's Future Sound and its other instructors. Students will produce original tracks for a compilation album with original artwork. The work runs from December 2, 2024 through May 26, 2025, and began before this board vote.

output.headline: Pays Bay Area Community Resources up to $10,062.50 for paid tech internships at Rudsdale High
output.summary: Bay Area Community Resources will create technology internships for about 35 students at Rudsdale Continuation High School and provide state student stipends for the hours they work. The agreement period began August 12, 2024, before this vote, and runs through June 30, 2025.

output.headline: Pays Bay Area Community Resources up to $60,000 for student and family support at Rudsdale High
output.summary: Bay Area Community Resources will provide direct services such as counseling, case management and mentoring to students, families and staff at Rudsdale Continuation High School. It will also run a Safety Risk Intervention Program and support newcomer students. The agreement period began August 12, 2024, before this vote, and runs through June 30, 2025.

output.headline: Pays Safe Passages up to $99,680 to coach after-school programs for young children
output.summary: Safe Passages will observe transitional kindergarten and kindergarten after-school programs, coach the lead agencies that run them, and host visits to its demonstration sites. It works through the Community Schools and Student Services Department. The agreement runs from January 8, 2025 through June 30, 2025.

output.headline: Pays Safe Passages up to $109,250 to train after-school staff serving young children
output.summary: Safe Passages will run four Professional Learning Communities (staff learning groups) for 50 after-school staff who serve transitional kindergarten and kindergarten students. The groups will share promising practices and culturally appropriate strategies. It works through the Community Schools and Student Services Department. The agreement runs from January 8, 2025 through June 30, 2025.

output.headline: Pays Oakland Public Education Fund up to $5,000 for an intern in the homeless student support program
output.summary: The Oakland Public Education Fund will administer stipends for an intern who helps the McKinney-Vento Program serve students and families experiencing housing instability. It works through the Community Schools and Student Services Department. The agreement period began November 11, 2024, before this vote, and runs through May 30, 2025.

output.headline: Pays SHC Services up to $400,000 for special education services through a nonpublic agency contract
output.summary: SHC Services, Supplemental Health Care will provide special education services required by students' Individualized Education Programs (IEPs), under a master contract for a nonpublic, nonsectarian school or agency. It works through the Special Education Department. The contract period began July 1, 2024, before this vote, and runs through June 30, 2025.

output.headline: Approves a no-cost WestEd study of the Illustrative Mathematics curriculum in grades 6-8, with student data sharing
output.summary: WestEd will study how the Illustrative Mathematics curriculum is used in grades 6-8 and how well it works. A separate data-sharing agreement sets the terms for the district sharing student data with WestEd and how WestEd must protect it. There is no cost to the district, and the term runs from August 1, 2024 through June 30, 2026.

output.headline: Partners with TransformCA at no cost on the Safe Routes to School program through June 2026
output.summary: TransformCA will recruit volunteer school champions at each school and at the district level to support participation in the Safe Routes to School Program, which promotes safe walking and biking education and events for all K-12 schools. There is no cost to the district. The term runs from July 1, 2024 through June 30, 2026, and began before this board vote.

output.headline: Accepts up to $1,280,000 from the state teaching commission for a school counseling residency program
output.summary: The district accepts a grant from the California Commission on Teacher Credentialing, at $320,000 per year for a total of up to $1,280,000. It supports a partnership with a college counseling preparation program to start or expand a school counseling residency program. The grant period began March 29, 2024, before this vote, and runs through June 30, 2027.

output.headline: Pays a consultant up to $45,000 to help Castlemont teachers use classroom smart boards
output.summary: An individual consultant will help Castlemont High School instructors load curriculum and plan class content on interactive Smart Boards and Promethean Boards, aiming to keep class time uninterrupted. The work runs from September 1, 2024 through June 30, 2025, and began before this board vote.

output.headline: Approves a no-cost partnership and student data sharing deal with Cal State East Bay for guaranteed admission
output.summary: The district is approving two agreements with California State University East Bay: a memorandum of understanding (MOU) and a data sharing agreement. They set up a Guaranteed Admissions Program for district students and cover how student data is shared and protected. Both run from January 1, 2025 through December 31, 2028 at no cost to the district.

output.headline: Pays NATEC International up to $4,400 for CPR training for Buildings & Grounds staff

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $4,400.00

output.summary: NATEC International will provide on-site CPR training to Buildings & Grounds staff through the Risk Management Department. The agreement runs December 1, 2024 through June 30, 2025, and the board is approving it after it began.

output.headline: Adds $74,000 to SCA Environmental's contract for school site environmental services
output.summary: This amendment adds $74,000 for SCA Environmental to provide environmental services that reduce risk at school sites, such as collecting samples like water lead tests and removing hazardous waste or debris during site recovery. The cap rises from $25,000 to $99,000. The contract period is unchanged, July 1, 2024 through June 30, 2025, and the board is approving the amendment after the fact.

The agreement runs from November 29, 2024 through June 1, 2025 and is paid from a community schools grant. The agreement is being approved after its start date.

output.headline: Pays Hanna Interpreting Services up to $1,000 for Mam and Arabic translation at Allendale Elementary

The agreement runs from January 7, 2025 through May 28, 2025 and is paid from a community schools grant. The agreement is being approved after its start date.

output.headline: Pays Playworks up to $26,674.22 to run recess games and conflict resolution at Manzanita Community Elementary

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $26,674.22

output.summary: Playworks will supervise games, teach strategies and set up conflict resolution systems during recess to support a positive schoolyard culture at Manzanita Community Elementary School. The agreement runs from August 19, 2024 through May 27, 2025 and is paid from a community schools grant. The agreement is being approved after its start date.

output.headline: Pays The Teaching Well up to $3,500 for staff wellness training at Emerson Elementary

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $3,500.00

output.summary: The Teaching Well will lead professional development sessions for staff at Emerson Elementary School on self-care, community care, socio-emotional skills and work-life balance. The agreement runs from November 18, 2024 through April 30, 2025 and is paid from educator effectiveness funds.

output.headline: Pays Bay Area Community Resources up to $29,971.88 for recess games and student council at Sankofa United

Elected students in grades two through five will discuss ways to make school safer and more fun. The agreement runs from August 16, 2024 through May 26, 2025 and is paid from a community schools grant.

output.headline: Pays Roda Leadership Development up to $20,000 to work on school culture at Esperanza Elementary

output.summary: Roda Leadership Development will work with school leaders, staff and community members to refine a plan for a more inclusive and affirming school culture, with a focus on pro-Black practices at Esperanza Elementary School. The agreement runs from October 7, 2024 through May 29, 2025. The agreement is being approved after its start date.

output.headline: Pays Wildcare up to $134.30 for a hands-on animal presentation at Esperanza Elementary

output.summary: Wildcare will visit Esperanza Elementary School and set up an interactive presentation where students can get close to animals. The goal is to build students' sense of responsibility toward protecting the planet. The agreement runs from November 20, 2024 through May 30, 2025. The agreement is being approved after its start date.

output.headline: Pays Children Rising up to $10,000 for one-on-one reading tutoring at Sankofa United Elementary

output.summary: Children Rising will provide intensive one-on-one literacy tutoring twice a week during school hours for students at Sankofa United Elementary School who struggle with foundational reading skills and are referred by school staff. The agreement runs from October 1, 2024 through May 29, 2025 and is paid from a community schools grant. The agreement is being approved after its start date.

output.summary: An individual consultant will update and clarify the district's Linked Learning standards so they better serve students and match district goals. Linked Learning is the district's career-themed high school program. The agreement runs from December 2, 2024 through June 30, 2025 and is paid from Measure H funds. The agreement is being approved after its start date.

output.headline: Pays 95 Percent Group up to $15,600 for on-site literacy instruction coaching

output.headline: Pays Living Jazz up to $9,297 for weekly dance classes at Thornhill Elementary

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $9,297.00

output.summary: Living Jazz will teach weekly dance classes for students at Thornhill Elementary School, ending with a performance showcase for the community and families. The agreement runs from January 7, 2025 through May 28, 2025 and is paid from Proposition 28 arts and music funds. The agreement is being approved after its start date.

output.headline: Adds $5,000 to Jensen Best's mindfulness training contract at Elmhurst United, raising it to $40,000
output.summary: This amendment adds $5,000 to an agreement with Jensen Best for virtual training and coaching for teachers and staff, called Effective Mindfulness, Building Responsive and Confident Educators (EMBRACE). The maximum rises from $35,000 to $40,000. The service period stays August 12, 2024 through May 30, 2025, and all other terms remain the same. The agreement is being approved after its start date.

output.headline: Approves Measure G1 carryover funding requests from 2023-24 for named schools
output.summary: The Board adopts Resolution No. 2425-0194, approving requests to carry over 2023-2024 Measure G1 funding for named schools. The Measure G1 oversight commission recommended it. The official text does not state a dollar amount or list the schools.
